sender: Daniel Wu, Director of Programs, Fengda Precision Industries
subject: Revised Dec-qtr iPhone build plan - the numbers
body:
Raj,

Good catching up in September. You asked me to ping you if the plan moved, and it did. We received the revised December-quarter iPhone build schedule on Monday. I'm giving you the numbers from my side of the program, not a forecast.

Total December-quarter builds across the final-assembly network, per the plan we were handed:
- Now about 91m units, vs. roughly 86m in the August plan
- Base iPhone 18: +7.5m vs. the August plan, with the extra volume mostly in India and one inland China site
- iPhone 18 Pro: flat
- iPhone 18 Pro Max: down about 2.5m, which matches what our camera and display partners are saying
- Folding model: unchanged at the pilot-scale volume pulled forward in August

It looks like Apple is pushing volume toward the base model, probably on carrier promos, trade-in strength in the U.S. and Europe, and softer Pro Max sell-through in China. Nobody told us why. We were only told to ramp the lines.

My own rough math on what this means for their numbers, which you can take or leave:
- Units: about 5m above where I think the Street sits
- Mix: the shift from Pro Max to base lowers blended ASP by roughly 3-4%
- Net: iPhone revenue maybe $2-3bn above consensus on volume, with some gross-margin dilution (my guess is 30-40bp for the quarter) because Pro Max carries the richest margin

Caveats: builds are not sell-through, plans have been revised again in mid-quarter before, and I cannot see Apple's channel inventory. Please do not forward this or attribute it to me.

Happy to talk Friday if you want to walk through it. I'm in Taipei until the 22nd.

Daniel
